questions.q: What is neuroplasticity, as the summary describes it?
a: The brain's ability to keep changing and learning for life
The brain's habit of storing memories in one place
The left brain's control over language and numbers
The mind's tendency to repeat childhood patterns
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines neuroplasticity as the brain changing and learning from birth to death.

questions.q: Which jobs does the summary assign to the left hemisphere?
a: Language, numbers, patterns and time
Sensory perception and the present moment
Balance, movement and spatial awareness
Emotion, intuition and big-picture calm
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the left side handles language and numbers and lets us see patterns and perceive time.

questions.q: What did Taylor feel once her left hemisphere went quiet?
a: Calm and connected, without fear of the future
Panicked and unable to recognize her body
Angry at the doctors who treated her
Numb and indifferent to everything around her
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes her right brain taking charge, leaving her neither scared of the present nor fearful of the future.

questions.q: What does the summary say mindfulness really is, according to Taylor?
a: A calm that already lives in the right brain
A skill only experienced meditators possess
A trait that some people are born without
A technique that requires years of practice
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that peace and calm come from the right brain, so mindfulness is already within everyone.

questions.q: What does Taylor mean by saying peace is only a thought away?
a: The right brain's calm is always available to visit
Peace arrives only after long meditation practice
Calm depends on removing every negative thought
Peace must be earned through good deeds
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the right brain's orientation is always there, available whenever you need an emotional breather.
